description: G3 and G6 (core src/editor/layout/composition/foliage.ts): trees and saplings gathered into groves by cell, set back from house walls (a tree 3 m, a sapling 1.5 m, corners and eaves included), undergrowth relaid at the trunks' feet (a tree filled to three plants), open undergrowth gathered into clumps, and the nearest-neighbour audit that reads a set as evenly spaced. Authored in core; every threshold has a case just inside and just past it. Plan frame: IR (x, z) metres.

sources.fixturesFrom: conformance/layout/ground-plan.json (copied byte for byte; the corpus test guards the copy)

cases.name: kinds: trees, saplings and undergrowth by the longest prefix; the rest are not foliage
cases.note: A sapling under the tree prefix is a sapling (the longer prefix wins); a flower, a rock and a lantern are not foliage.

cases.name: set-back: a tree 2.85 m from a wall is set back to 3.2 m
cases.note: G6: no tree 1-2 m from a wall. Just inside the tree's 3 m set-back: moved straight out to 3 m plus the 0.2 m margin; a lone tree, so no grove pull, and its foot filled to three plants.

cases.name: set-back: a tree 3.15 m from a wall stays
cases.note: Just past the 3 m set-back: kept where it stands.

cases.name: set-back: a sapling 1.425 m off a house's corner is set back along the diagonal
cases.note: G6: no sapling at a corner. The corner counts: just inside the sapling's 1.5 m set-back, moved out to 1.7 m from the corner.

cases.name: set-back: a sapling 1.575 m off a house's corner stays
cases.note: Just past the 1.5 m set-back.

cases.name: set-back: a sapling under the eaves and a tree inside the outline are both stood out
cases.note: A sapling 0.4 m off the wall (under the eaves) goes to 1.7 m; a tree whose trunk is inside the outline goes out across the nearest wall to 3.2 m.

cases.name: set-aside: a tree between two houses 4 m apart has no spot
cases.note: Set back 3.2 m from the nearer house (ties by id) it stands 0.8 m from the other: `walls`, set aside, never left by a wall.

cases.name: set-aside: a tree whose set-back lands on a road
cases.note: Stood out to 3.2 m it would be on the road: `on-strip`, set aside.

cases.name: groves: an even grid of eight trees gathers into groves
cases.note: G3: trees 6 m apart on a grid read as evenly spaced (cv 0). Each 12 m cell pulls its trees half way to its jittered middle; the audit after is not even.

cases.name: groves: a pull into a lot is not made
cases.note: Two trees of one cell whose pull would end inside a lot keep their spots (`pull-blocked`).

cases.name: undergrowth: a tuft 3.8 m from a trunk is relaid at its foot
cases.note: G3: undergrowth at the trees' feet. Just inside the 4 m reach: the tuft is the tree's first plant, and two fills complete the foot; a rock is not foliage and is left.

cases.name: undergrowth: a tuft 4.2 m from a trunk stays in the open
cases.note: Just past the 4 m reach: the tuft is open undergrowth, alone in its clump cell, kept; the tree is filled with three.

cases.name: undergrowth: a sapling's foot takes what is near and is not filled; spots on a path are skipped
cases.note: Two ferns by a sapling go to its foot (a sapling is not filled); the tree beside a path skips the spiral spots on it.

cases.name: clumps: twelve tufts scattered evenly gather into clumps
cases.note: G3: tufts on a 2 m grid (even) with no trunk near: each 5 m cell of two or more pulls them 0.6 of the way to its jittered middle; the audit after is not even.

cases.name: audit: neighbour distances varying by 0.2375 read as evenly spaced
cases.note: Four corners of a rectangle (1 m by the side that makes each corner's three neighbour distances vary by a cv of 0.2375): just inside 0.25, even.

cases.name: audit: neighbour distances varying by 0.2625 do not
cases.note: The rectangle drawn out to a cv of 0.2625: just past 0.25, not even.

cases.name: audit: a set of like clumps is not even
cases.note: Four clumps of three, alike inside (0.8 m) and 10 m apart: the first neighbour alone would read them as even; pooled with the third, they are not.

cases.name: audit: three are no pattern
cases.note: Fewer than four props are never read as even.

cases.name: set-aside: a tree set back to 2.85 m from a second house's wall is set aside
cases.note: A tree 2 m from house-a's wall is set back to 3.2 m from it, which is 2.85 m from house-b's wall: inside house-b's 3 m set-back, so it is set aside (`walls`).

cases.name: set-back: a tree set back to 3.15 m from a second house's wall stands there
cases.note: As the case before with house-b 0.3 m farther: the set-back spot is 3.15 m from its wall, outside its 3 m set-back, so the tree is set back.

cases.name: set-aside: a sapling set back to 1.425 m from a second house's wall is set aside
cases.note: A sapling 1 m from house-a's wall is set back to 1.7 m from it, 1.425 m from house-b's wall: inside a sapling's 1.5 m set-back of house-b, set aside (`walls`).

cases.name: set-back: a sapling set back to 1.575 m from a second house's wall stands there
cases.note: As the case before with house-b 0.15 m farther: 1.575 m off its wall is outside a sapling's set-back (a tree's 3 m does not apply to a sapling), so it is set back.

cases.name: set-back: a tree equally near two houses' corners is set back from the lower id
cases.note: A tree 2 m from a corner of house-b and of house-a (listed b first), 20 degrees apart: it is set back from house-a, the lower id, along the line from that corner, and stands 3.15 m from house-b's.

cases.name: set-back: a tree exactly 3 m from a wall is kept
cases.note: As the 3.15 m case with the tree 3 m off the wall: the set-back itself is far enough, so it stays.

cases.name: set-back: a tree exactly on a wall is stood out from the house's middle
cases.note: A tree at (8, 4), on house-a's wall: there is no way out from the wall's nearest point, so it is stood out along the line from the house's middle through that point, to 3.2 m off the wall at (11.2, 4).
